message.content: {"output_action": "CREATE", "skill_draft": {"name": "verify_directional_signs_in_opacification", "description": "When interpreting hemithorax opacification ('white-out'), explicitly verify the direction of mediastinal shift before concluding the etiology.", "applicable_conditions": "Any diagnostic task involving unilateral lung opacity or loss of lung volume where differential diagnosis depends on mass effect versus volume loss.", "branch": "general", "tool_name": null, "task_category": ["detection", "localization", "characterization", "reasoning"], "required_tools": [], "risk_level": "high", "core_action": "If you observe unilateral hemithorax opacification: (1) Explicitly identify the direction of mediastinal/tracheal shift relative to the opacity; (2) If shift is contralateral (away), prioritize space-occupying lesions (e.g., massive effusion, large mass); (3) If shift is ipsilateral (toward), prioritize volume-loss conditions (e.g., atelectasis, fibrosis); (4) Do not default to 'effusion' for all white-outs without confirming the shift direction."}, "patch_target_id": null, "patch_section": null, "patch_content": null}
